title: Parameter quotient diagram and its residue colimit
statement: Let k be a field, B a commutative local k-algebra and t:Fin d→B a tuple generating its maximal ideal. Let I be a nonempty directed partial order, C:I→CommAlgCat k a diagram, τ a natural family k[X_i]→C_a and β a natural family C_a→B whose composites are evaluation at t. Assume every τ_a is smooth on affine spectra and β is a colimit cocone in commutative rings. Then each C_a is nonzero regular Noetherian with τ_a(X_i) a regular sequence. There is a compatible diagram D of the actual parameter quotients (with equivalences identifying q_a with their quotient projections), maps q:C→D and γ:D→B/n, every D_a is nonzero regular Noetherian smooth over k, and each Spec(q_a) is a regular closed immersion of codimension d. The cocone γ is a ring colimit and γ_a∘q_a=residue∘β_a. No regularity or completeness of B and no prime-field condition on k is assumed.

source.place: Algebra, Tags 00T4 and 00TA; Algebra, Tag 07NF; quotient universal properties; original node steps 7–9.

proof.text: For each stage define K_a as the span of τ_a(X_i). Naturality of τ makes transitions preserve K_a, so quotient maps construct a functor D_a=C_a/K_a and the natural quotient q. Compatibility of β with evaluation and generation of the maximal ideal show that residue∘β_a kills K_a; quotient lifts construct γ and its naturality.

The maps γ_a to the nonzero residue field make D_a nonzero. Apply the single-stage smooth polynomial parameter lemma to obtain regularity, the stage sequence, smoothness of D_a over the base, and the codimension-d quotient immersion. The normalization equivalence is the identity.

Given a cocone on D with vertex R, compose its legs with q. The supplied colimit property gives a unique ring map g:B→R. For any one stage a, evaluating its colimit factorization on τ_a(X_i) shows g(t_i)=0. Thus g kills the maximal ideal and has a unique quotient lift from the residue field. The factorization equations follow from the colimit equations before quotienting, and uniqueness follows by the original colimit hom-ext principle and surjectivity of the residue projection. The displayed commuting square holds by construction.

lean.statement: theorem smooth_parameter_quotient_diagram (k₀ B : Type u) [Field k₀] [CommRing B] [Algebra k₀ B] [IsLocalRing B] (d : ℕ) (t : Fin d → B) (hgen : Ideal.span (Set.range t) = maximalIdeal B) (I : Type u) [PartialOrder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] [Nonempty I] (C : I ⥤ CommAlgCat.{u} k₀) (τ : (Functor.const I).obj (CommAlgCat.of k₀ (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k₀)) ⟶ C) (β : C ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj (CommAlgCat.of k₀ B)) (hcompat : ∀ a : I, (β.app a).hom.comp (τ.app a).hom = MvPolynomial.aeval t) (hsmooth : ∀ a : I, Smooth (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (τ.app a).hom.toRingHom))) (hcolim : Nonempty (IsColimit ((forget₂ (CommAlgCat.{u} k₀) CommRingCat.{u}).mapCocone { pt := CommAlgCat.of k₀ B, ι := β }))) : (∀ a : I, Nontrivial (C.obj a) ∧ IsRegularRing (C.obj a) ∧ RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular (C.obj a) (List.ofFn fun i : Fin d ↦ (τ.app a).hom (MvPolynomial.X i))) ∧ ∃ (D : I ⥤ CommAlgCat.{u} k₀) (q : C ⟶ D) (γ : D ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj (CommAlgCat.of k₀ (ResidueField B))), (∀ a : I, ∃ e : (C.obj a ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range fun i : Fin d ↦ (τ.app a).hom (MvPolynomial.X i))) ≃ₐ[k₀] D.obj a, ∀ x : C.obj a, e (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span (Set.range fun i : Fin d ↦ (τ.app a).hom (MvPolynomial.X i))) x) = (q.app a).hom x) ∧ (∀ a : I, Nontrivial (D.obj a) ∧ IsRegularRing (D.obj a) ∧ Smooth (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k₀ (D.obj a)))) ∧ IsRegularClosedImmersionWithCodimension (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (q.app a).hom.toRingHom)) (fun _ ↦ d)) ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit ((forget₂ (CommAlgCat.{u} k₀) CommRingCat.{u}).mapCocone { pt := CommAlgCat.of k₀ (ResidueField B), ι := γ })) ∧ (∀ a : I, (γ.app a).hom.toRingHom.comp (q.app a).hom.toRingHom = (residue B).comp (β.app a).hom.toRingHom)
